module.title: Bacterial Kdp potassium-homeostasis system
module.description: A reusable bacterial module coupling KdpD/KdpE phosphorelay control to the high-affinity KdpFABC potassium pump. KdpD senses conditions associated with potassium limitation and phosphorylates KdpE, activated KdpE promotes kdpFABC transcription, and the membrane KdpFABC complex couples ATP hydrolysis to potassium uptake. Constitutive potassium channels and lower-affinity uptake systems are outside this module.

module.notes: The Kdp system is conserved across phylogenetically distant bacteria (Proteobacteria, Firmicutes, Actinobacteria, Cyanobacteria) and also occurs in some haloarchaea, so the module is species-neutral. Escherichia coli K-12 KdpFABC/KdpDE is the canonical, structurally and biochemically characterized system and seeds every PAINT node used here; Pseudomonas putida KT2440 provides a second, sequence-inferred proteobacterial implementation, and a Desulfovibrio KdpB adds a deltaproteobacterial pump exemplar. The module context is kept at Bacteria because the archaeal members are known here only from PANTHER membership, not from characterization. The KdpD/KdpE sensor and response-regulator steps are grouped as an inner phosphorelay bundle that `conforms_to` MODULE:two_component_relay WITH_DEVIATIONS: it is a simple two-tier system with direct His-to-Asp transfer and no histidine-phosphotransfer (Hpt, GO:0009927) protein, so the validator's tier-count, tier-function and topology advisories for the missing Hpt tier are expected. The pump output remains a free extension outside the conforming bundle. KdpE carries two annotons, matching the two core functions its gene reviews keep separate: the receiver-domain phosphotransfer (GO:0000156) inside the bundle, and cis-regulatory DNA binding (GO:0000987) driving transcription as a sibling part outside it. Fusing the phosphorelay function with the transcription process would assert that GO:0000156 is the activity performing GO:0045893, which neither the gene reviews nor the ontology support. The environmental input to KdpD integrates potassium limitation, ionic strength and membrane-state signals differently among bacteria, so the first role is described conservatively; truncated cyanobacterial KdpD-like proteins lack the transmitter region and fall outside the sensor kinase role. KdpC and KdpF are retained as pump components but are not assigned independent catalytic molecular functions. KdpF stabilization is grounded by E. coli biochemical evidence; conservation of that quantitative contribution in other bacteria remains inferential. KdpF is grounded on NCBIfam:TIGR02115 (integrated in InterPro IPR011726) because this 29-residue membrane peptide has no PANTHER family assignment; both KdpF exemplars carry the TIGR02115 match. The KdpE family (PTHR48111) is a broad OmpR/PhoB-type response-regulator family; it is grounded at the KdpE subfamily SF50 because target genes and regulatory sign differ between subfamilies. PAINT and GOA assign the Kdp subunits to GO:1903103 potassium:proton antiporter complex; the family and gene reviews treat that as a mis-mapping of GO:0031004, since KdpFABC is an ATP-driven importer.

document.description: KdpB is the catalytic ATP-binding subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake system in N. vulgaris Hildenborough (DVU_3338). As a P-type ATPase (EC 7.2.2.6), KdpB hydrolyzes ATP and forms an aspartyl-phosphate intermediate (Asp302) during the E1/E2 catalytic cycle, driving K+ translocation across the inner membrane. The KdpFABC complex is induced under severe K+ limitation and provides high-affinity K+ uptake (apparent Km ~2 uM). KdpB couples ATP hydrolysis to conformational changes that drive K+ transport through a ~40 A tunnel from the KdpA selectivity filter to the cytoplasmic release site in KdpB.

document.description: KdpA is the potassium-binding and potassium-translocating subunit of KdpFABC, the inducible high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the bacterial inner membrane, which is expressed when external K+ falls to micromolar levels. KdpA is a ten-transmembrane-helix member of the superfamily of potassium transporters (SKT), built from four M1PM2 repeats around a KcsA-like selectivity filter that binds dehydrated K+ and confers the high affinity and K+/Rb+ discrimination of the system. KdpA itself has no ATPase activity: energy is supplied by the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, and structures show an intramembrane tunnel that carries K+ from the KdpA selectivity filter to the canonical cation site of KdpB, with the accessory single-span subunits KdpC and KdpF stabilizing the complex.

KdpC acts as a catalytic chaperone at the KdpB nucleotide-binding loop. KdpB activity is inhibited by phosphorylation of Ser162 in the TGES motif of the A domain.

document.description: KdpC is the small accessory subunit of KdpFABC, the inducible high-affinity ATP-driven potassium uptake pump of the bacterial inner membrane, and is required together with KdpA and KdpB for a functional system. KdpC has a single transmembrane helix and a soluble domain of novel fold; crystal and cryo-EM structures place this domain on the periplasmic side, where it is held against periplasmic loops of the K+-selective subunit KdpA near the entrance of its selectivity filter, and KdpC (with KdpF) stabilizes the KdpA-KdpB partnership. KdpC neither hydrolyzes ATP (a KdpB function) nor forms the K+ pathway (a KdpA function). Earlier biochemical work proposed that KdpC acts as a "catalytic chaperone" that binds ATP and raises the nucleotide affinity of KdpB, but the periplasmic placement of its soluble domain in the structures is difficult to reconcile with direct contact with the cytoplasmic nucleotide-binding domain of KdpB.

document.description: KdpD is the inner-membrane sensor of the E. coli KdpD/KdpE two-component system that controls the high-affinity K+ uptake pump KdpFABC. The 894-residue homodimer has a large cytoplasmic N-terminal input region (containing a Walker A/B atypical kinase domain and a Usp domain), four transmembrane helices, and a cytoplasmic C-terminal transmitter (GAF, DHp and HATPase_c domains). Under K+ limitation or salt stress KdpD autophosphorylates His673 in trans and transfers the phosphoryl group to KdpE, which then activates kdpFABC transcription; it also dephosphorylates KdpE~P, and the kinase/phosphatase balance responds to both extracellular and intracellular K+. Its activity is modulated by UspC (scaffold under salt stress) and dephosphorylated IIA(Ntr). At high K+ the N-terminal atypical serine kinase domain phosphorylates KdpB Ser162, inhibiting the KdpFABC pump post-translationally.

KdpD is the phosphatase that returns KdpE~P to the inactive state.

document.preferred_name: KdpA potassium-binding and translocating subunit of KdpFABC
document.summary: KdpA is the potassium-selective, membrane-embedded subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex found in many bacteria and some archaea. It belongs to the superfamily of K+ transporters (SKT) and carries a channel-like selectivity filter formed by four M1-P-M2 repeats. KdpA binds periplasmic K+ and passes it through an intramembrane tunnel to the membrane domain of the P-type ATPase subunit KdpB, which releases it into the cytoplasm at the expense of ATP. KdpA does not hydrolyse ATP itself: the complete reaction of P-type potassium transport is a property of the assembled KdpFABC complex, to which KdpA contributes substrate selection and translocation.
document.coherence_reason: PANTHER resolves a single subfamily (SF2) and a single PAINT node for this family. Every reviewed member is annotated as KdpA of a Kdp operon, and the selectivity-filter architecture is shared. There are no known divergent paralog groups; the main interpretive caution is that the transporter activity is a complex-level activity to which KdpA contributes.

document.summary: KdpB is the catalytic, pump-like subunit of the KdpFABC high-affinity potassium uptake complex of bacteria and some archaea. document.summary: KdpD is the membrane-bound sensor histidine kinase that, with the response regulator KdpE, controls expression of the kdpFABC potassium-uptake operon. Some cyanobacterial members are truncated and lack the transmitter region.

document.summary: A large family of two-component response regulators with an N-terminal receiver domain and a C-terminal winged helix-turn-helix (OmpR/PhoB-type) DNA-binding output domain. Phosphotransfer from a cognate sensor histidine kinase to a conserved receiver aspartate drives dimerization and binding to promoter regions, so that each regulator controls the regulon of its own signalling pathway. Characterized members include E. coli OmpR, PhoB, PhoP, CpxR, ArcA, BaeR, BasR, CreB, TorR and KdpE, Pseudomonas AlgR and streptococcal WalR. The receiver-to-DNA-binding mechanism is shared, but regulon, target promoters, regulatory sign and physiological process are set by the subfamily.
document.coherence_reason: The receiver-domain phosphorelay activity, cis-regulatory DNA binding and transcriptional regulation are shared family-wide and supported by many seeds in PANTHER's 49 subfamilies. Specific biology is not shared: KdpE (SF50) activates the kdpFABC potassium-pump operon, OmpR (SF4) is a dual activator and repressor of porin genes, ArcA (SF55) controls aerobic respiration genes, and so on. The direction of regulation and any process more specific than transcription regulation must therefore be assigned per subfamily.
